messages.subject: RE: Stacked bar chart with negative values on one side of axis?
parts:
Dear Matt,

Are you OK with dodge?  It shows all the negative bars.

 

ggplot(cr.sd.df, aes(x=Group)) +

  geom_bar(data=subset(cr.sd.df, variable=Factor),

           aes(y=value, fill=Factor),stat="identity", position="dodge")

 

Or, if you use alpha transparency, you can see it is overwrapping.

 

ggplot(cr.sd.df, aes(x=Group)) +

  geom_bar(data=subset(cr.sd.df, variable=Factor),

           aes(y=value, fill=Factor),stat="identity", alpha=0.3)

 

 

From: ggp...@googlegroups.com [mailto:ggp...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of Matt Considine
Sent: Tuesday, May 21, 2013 6:49 PM
To: ggp...@googlegroups.com
Subject: Stacked bar chart with negative values on one side of axis?

 

Hi,
I have tried to find the answer to this in the archives and on Google via searches for "back-to-back" barcharts, but am not having much luck.  So apologies in advance if the solution is simple.

I would like to create a stacked bar chart that shows negative values on one side of the x (or y, if horizontal) axis.  The dataframe is this

cr.sd,df <- structure(list(Factor = structure(c(10L, 11L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 5L,
3L, 8L, 6L, 7L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 5L, 3L, 8L, 6L, 7L,
9L, 10L, 11L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 5L, 3L, 8L, 6L, 7L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 4L,
1L, 2L, 5L, 3L, 8L, 6L, 7L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 5L, 3L,
8L, 6L, 7L, 9L), .Label = c("f1", "f2", "f3",
"f4", "f5", "f6", "f7", "f8", "f9", "f10",
"f11"), class = "factor"), Group = structure(c(2L, 2L,
2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L,
3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 4L,
4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 5L,
5L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 5L), .Label = c("A", "B",
"C", "D", "E"), class = "factor"),
    value = c(0.0328546884096332, 0.000852504698436131, -0.000173715974304095,
    0.00681930186975633, 0.00126027725934588, 0.0023783731539428,
    0.000153862706497096, -0.0007320325628755, 0.000575200971239038,
    -2.38782918164678e-05, 0.001964098479893, -0.000996355853310439,
    0.000944143854895036, 0.00102003085323505, 0.00189789834714615,
    0.00027254805380872, -5.20831258457188e-05, 5.85462886042536e-05,
    0.00041548641132429, 0.000943018440975702, 0.00120023436244587,
    0.0046920216859867, 0.00907225512622178, -0.000667263945848423,
    -0.000828762649237377, 0.000722028515916353, 0.00564288769227779,
    -0.00132964106808853, -1.51169425196072e-05, 0.000994399684376369,
    -7.28913967351872e-05, -0.00277052615893433, 0.0122652725786377,
    0.000705526280942326, 0.000140936092846917, -0.00266550877376146,
    0.00868348939825975, 0.00262917746073491, 0.0013770329808627,
    0.000543180000138685, 0.00122351156915728, 0.000855533244945603,
    0.00120401868228823, 0.00260517893375856, 0.0114975907205063,
    0.000687019815957743, -0.00221721087514512, 0.00685703679071788,
    0.0019446347332894, 0.000929153339322914, 0.000238324158101547,
    0.000326000088858993, 0.000710236931185339, 0.000550723775793639,
    0.000943478391424703)), .Names = c("Factor", "Group", "value"
), row.names = c(NA, -55L), class = "data.frame")

And the code I am running is :

ggplot(cr.sd.df, aes(x=Group)) +
  geom_bar(data=subset(cr.sd.df, variable=Factor),
           aes(y=value, fill=Factor),stat="identity")

Unfortunately, this seems to hides some of the factors that have negative values behind the first factor that has a positive value.  This can be seen if one runs the same code but plots the absolute values :

ggplot(cr.sd.df, aes(x=Group)) +
  geom_bar(data=subset(cr.sd.df, variable=Factor),
           aes(y=abs(value), fill=Factor),stat="identity")

A before-and-after comparison shows which values (actually negative) I would like stacked on the other side of the axis.

The solutions I found posted for back-to-back barcharts all seemed to assume that the data was in series that could be separately identified as being on one side or the other of the axis.  But in this case that is not known ahead of time.

Can someone point out a solution?

Thanks in advance (and apologies for any lapses in posting etiquette),
Matt

messages.subject: RE: Stacked bar chart with negative values on one side of axis?
parts:
Thank you for the reply and the thoughts. "dodge" would work but then
I lose what I think is an intuition provided by the stacked bars, namely
the sense of contribution within each Group.

Alpha transparency didn't seem to work, as I thought the negative bars
were still being masked.

A solution I've come up with that is not as elegant as I was hoping for
but which seems to work is to break out the positive and negative groups
into two datasets.

cr.sd.pos <- cr.sd
cr.sd.pos[which(cr.sd<0)]=0
cr.sd.neg <- cr.sd
cr.sd.neg[which(cr.sd>=0)]=0
cr.sd.pos.df <- melt(cr.sd.pos,varnames=c("Factor","Group"))
cr.sd.neg.df <- melt(cr.sd.neg,varnames=c("Factor","Group"))
ggplot(cr.sd.df, aes(x=Group)) +
geom_bar(data=subset(cr.sd.pos.df, variable=Factor),
aes(y=value, fill=Factor),stat="identity") +
geom_bar(data=subset(cr.sd.neg.df, variable=Factor),
aes(y=value, fill=Factor),stat="identity") +
scale_fill_manual(values=rainbow(12))

Still, if there were a better way to accomplish this - or I am
completely missing the boat on a set of options, functions, etc. I'd be
interested to hear about it.

Thanks again,
Matt

It is interesting that it works when you split the dataset for negative and positive.
I think you can write less code as below:

ggplot(cr.sd.df, aes(x=Group, y=value, fill=Factor)) +
geom_bar(data=subset(cr.sd.df, value>=0),stat="identity") +
geom_bar(data=subset(cr.sd.df, value<0),stat="identity")

Kaori
